  whether you stole one, not its kind; they are told which kind they lost. If they have no tokens, nothing
  happens and they aren't told. A steal from a player who dies that night still takes the token and counts (R10).
  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Vulture
  Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and your threshold or fewer players
  are alive, counting yourself. The game then ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles
  that never block wins still count, R1). Your threshold starts at 2.
  Night: may visit another player. If they die that night (by any cause, end-of-night effects included), you are
  told at the end of the night that they died and their role (exact-role check, R19; nothing more if a Mortician
  cleaned them), and you get the first of these power-ups you don't have yet: +1 to your threshold, Standard
  Defense, +1 to your threshold, Strong Defense, then +1 to your threshold for each later one. Your threshold
  never goes above max(floor(N/3), 2), where N is the number of players at the start of the game; a power-up that
  would raise it further is skipped. If they don't die, nothing happens and you are told so.

Decoy
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you die at night. You lose if you die by Day or the game ends with you alive.
  If an attack killed you at night, the next Day's announcements say you were the Decoy and name 3 players: every
  player whose attack would have killed you on its own (3 of them at random if there were more), then random other
  players alive at the start of that Day to make 3 (fewer if not enough are left). The names are in random order,
  and the announcement doesn't say how many of them attacked you. Your cause of death and last will show as usual.

=== PART 7: TRAITS ===

R24 (Traits)
Some players also have a trait: an extra ability on top of their role. You are told your own trait at the start
(except a hidden trait, which says so); nobody else is told, not even your teammates, and whether a game has any
traits is secret. Investigations never see traits: they report roles and alignments only. A trait stays with you if
your role changes. Traits are always true: a Roleplayer's trait is real even though its role isn't. A player may
have more than one trait, but never the same one twice. Each trait below says who can get it (Who), whether it is
hidden from its holder (Hidden), whether at most one player in a game has it (Unique), what it does (Effect) and
which traits nobody holds together with it (Never with). A trait's night action is used in addition to your role's
own, and a role-block stops it too.

--- Village players only ---

Martyr
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the announcement of your death also says you were a Martyr and names every player whose
  vote counted as Guilty in your trial. Your role stays hidden. A Martyr who dies any other way shows nothing.

Cursed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the
  night you died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks,
  so the victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night. Its cause is
  "a curse". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Avenger
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack would have killed you is dealt a Basic Attack (an
  Astral Visit) that same night. Defense and protection apply as usual (R3); a kill's cause is "Avenger". Attacks
  that weren't fatal on their own, and deaths by Day, set nothing off. It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't
  stop it.

Kindred
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn up to two random other players whose votes counted the
  same way as the vote you cast (if fewer did, you learn that). It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Remorseful
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Guilty in a trial and that player is hanged and was Village (their true alignment), you die at
  once; the cause is "remorse". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks
  counts it.
  Never with: Zealot.

Ashamed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Innocent in a trial and that player is hanged and wasn't Village (their true alignment: Yakuza
  or Neutral), you die at once; the cause is "shame". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing
  that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Merciful or Turncoat.

Faultline
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn one random other player whose vote counted as Guilty
  and one whose vote counted as Innocent (if all the others voted one way, you learn that). It needs no action, so a
  role-block doesn't stop it.

Notorious
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19). Checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count,
  aren't fooled.
  Never with: Turncoat.

Stolen Blade
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may attack another living player with a stolen Katana: a Standard Attack,
  besides your role's own action. It is an action and a visit by you, and it looks exactly like the Yakuza's Katana
  attack: a kill's cause is "Katana", and a surviving target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana.
  You learn only whether it killed. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Paranoid
  Who: Village players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/4, you are told you were attacked and survived, though nobody attacked
  you. The made-up attack is the Katana's 2/3 of the time, and otherwise a Vigilante's or a Serial Killer's (always
  the Katana's when neither role can be in the game); it is worded like a real one. Nothing else happens: it isn't a
  visit or an attack, and nobody else learns of it.
  Never with: Oblivious.

Turncoat
  Who: Village players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise, even if the Village wins.
  Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19); checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count, see you
  as Good. You stay Village in every other way: you aren't in the Yakuza's chat or Katana votes, you don't know who
  the Yakuza are, and they aren't told about you. The game's end ignores you, like a role that never blocks wins
  (R1): it ends when the other living players are all Village or all Yakuza.
  Never with: Ashamed, Notorious, Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Spiteful.

Spiteful
  Who: Village players only, except a Saint.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: If you are hanged, from then on you win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise,
  even if the Village wins. Until then you win with the Village as usual, and dying any other way changes nothing.
  Nobody is told you switched, and your will is revealed as usual.
  Never with: Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Turncoat.

--- Yakuza players only ---

Spare Blade
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may make one extra Katana attack on another living player, whoever holds the
  Katana and besides its own attack (which the Yakuza still choose as usual, R8). It is Standard, an action and a
  visit by you, and its target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana. A role-block stops it, and then
  it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed or Berserker.

Usurper
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win while you are the only Yakuza alive, and then you take the win alone: the
  other Yakuza, alive or dead, don't win. If the Yakuza win with another Yakuza alive, they win and you don't. Your
  teammates aren't told.
  Never with: Selfish or Selfless.

Shaky
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Every Katana attack you make (the Katana's own while you hold it, or a Spare Blade attack) is level None,
  so it never kills (R3); it is still an attack and a visit.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Katana Master.

Katana Expert
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its own attack Strong instead of Standard.
  Choose it with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at
  the end of that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along
  with the attack, and it isn't used up.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Master or Shaky.

Katana Master
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Like Katana Expert, but the attack is Divine, which no Defense, protection, trap or charm stops.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Shaky.

Berserker
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its attack rampage: besides its own attack, it
  makes a Standard Katana attack on every other player who visits its target that night, whatever their faction.
  These attacks on visitors aren't visits, and Astral Visits aren't visits, so their makers aren't attacked. Choose it
  with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at the end of
  that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along with the
  attack, and it isn't used up. Each attacked player learns only that they were attacked with the Katana; you learn
  how many players the rampage attacked and how many of those attacks killed, not who the visitors were.
  Never with: Katana Expert, Katana Master, Shaky or Spare Blade.

--- Village and Yakuza players only ---

Armed
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at another living player: a Basic Attack. It is an
  action and a visit, and a role-blocked shot isn't used up. You learn only whether it killed its target. A kill's
  cause is "a hidden gun".
  Never with: Spare Blade or Stolen Blade.

Bonded
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random Village or Yakuza player are bonded, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role or faction). If either of you dies, the other dies of heartbreak at once (its cause is
  "heartbreak"). Heartbreak isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Rival.

Rival
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random player of your own faction are rivals, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role). Each of you wins only if your faction wins and the other has died by the end; whether you are
  alive doesn't matter. Your faction's win doesn't change.
  Never with: Bonded, Spiteful or Turncoat.

Selfish
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are alive at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you
  just don't share it if you died.
  Never with: Selfless, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

Selfless
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are dead at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you just
  don't share it if you're alive.
  Never with: Selfish, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

--- Any player ---

Grudge
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the next night one random player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial, among
  those alive when that night begins, is dealt a Standard Attack (an Astral Visit). Defense and protection apply as
  usual. A kill's cause is "a grudge". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Loud
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You earn 1.5 times the usual speaking budget each round, and your cap is 1.5 times the usual (R22). Your
  prices and trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Curt
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: The length part of your message prices (R22) is doubled, so long messages cost you much more; each
  message's base fee, nominations and your trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Confidant
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Once per game, on one of your own Day turns, you may send one private message hidden: nobody else is told
  it was sent, and the public ledger doesn't count it. Its recipient sees that it was hidden. Players who hear
  private messages (e.g. the Wiretap) still hear it, also marked hidden.

Zealot
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Every Guilty/Innocent trial vote you cast counts as Guilty, whatever you vote, including in your own
  trial. Your nomination (Yes/No) votes are unchanged. Your private reminder shows both the vote you cast and how it
  counted, and everything that reports how you voted (e.g. the Auditor, a Martyr's announcement) uses the vote as
  counted. A Fixer's reversal doesn't change it.
  Never with: Merciful or Remorseful.

Merciful
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Like Zealot, but your trial votes always count as Innocent.
  Never with: Ashamed or Zealot.

Drowsy
  Who: Any player whose role has a night action and can be role-blocked.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/2, you are role-blocked (R9) with no blocker. On those nights you are
  told you were role-blocked, as with any role-block.

Stocked
  Who: Any player whose role starts with tokens and can ever have more than it starts with.
  Effect: You start with one more of each kind of token your role starts with.

Disguised
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You are told a Village role (never your own), drawn at the start. Every exact-role check (R18) sees you as
  that role instead of yours, alive or dead; alignment checks still see your true alignment.

Narrow Escape
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Once per game, on the first night an attack that isn't Divine would kill you (after Defense, protection,
  traps and charms), you survive: every non-Divine attack on you that night fails instead. It works like Strong
  Defense on every night until then, so a night when nothing would have killed you (e.g. a Medic stopped the attack)
  doesn't use it up. Divine Attacks and deaths by Day aren't stopped. You are told about the failed attacks as for
  any others (R3).

Oblivious
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: You are never told about an attack you survive.
  Never with: Paranoid.

Sleepwalker
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every night you visit one random other living player, besides any action of your own; code draws it, and
  you aren't told whom. It does nothing but visit: anything that sees or reacts to visits (R6), such as a Tracker, a
  Lookout or a Veteran's alert, counts it. It isn't optional, but a role-block stops it (R7).

---

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- Track Arsonist douses with set_status key 'doused' value true. An ignite uses up every douse: clear 'doused' on everyone it hit, survivors included (rules: Arsonist). Don't tell anyone they were doused: code tells the doused players who should know.
- An Auditor who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the audit op; code tells them the player's votes from the Day. Don't tell() the Auditor anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Bounty Hunter's attack is a Strong Attack that spends its attack token: pass by=<the Bounty Hunter> on the kill op, since code credits its bounties from the killers. Code tells it which bounties it claimed or lost and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about bounties.
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks, unless it was role-blocked (R9; set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder, a Kitsune's release for the Kitsune; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- Mirror Maker: a Mirror Maker who acted on another player (and wasn't role-blocked) placed a mirror on them (it spends a token). Resolve it right after any fox charm (Kitsune) and before traps and Defense: use the mirror op with every non-Divine Attack on the mirrored player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert or an Enforcer's attack), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}, [] if none. Don't list the attacks code reflects (below). Code says which attacks the mirror stops (all of them, except one a fox charm already swallowed): treat each as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), so traps and Medics on that player have nothing left to stop. For each stopped visit, code says it is reflected: resolve it as an Attack of the same level on its attacker (an Astral Visit, never reflected again: a mirror on the attacker just stops it), against their Defense, protection, traps and charms as usual. If it kills, kill with exactly the stopped attack's cause, by the Mirror Maker, katana false (a reflected Katana attack reads as a Katana death); a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Mirror Maker. Several mirrors on one player: one op each, every one listing all the attacks; they stop the attacks together. Code tells the Mirror Maker its result; don't tell() it.
- Oathsworn: an Oathsworn who spent its token (and wasn't role-blocked) marks its target: use the swear op, which spends the token; it is a visit to the target only, and nothing else happens that night (nobody is told). On the next Night, if the Oathsworn is dead when the Night begins, code says so in tonight's notes: call record_visits first, then the fulfil_oath op ({op:'fulfil_oath', by: <the dead Oathsworn>}): code lists the Divine Attacks, cause 'a blood oath', on the marked player and on every other player who visited them tonight (Astral Visits, not visits; Astral visitors aren't hit). Divine Attacks beat every Defense and ignore protection, traps, charms, mirrors and Narrow Escape, so each one kills.

Their own actions aren't visits and have no effect: no other role sees or is affected by them, so never put them in record_visits (rules: Roleplayer). Exception: for a role whose results code gives (named in tonight's notes), handle them as a real user of that role and don't invent anything.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- Cursed (a trait, R24): for a Cursed player who died today or dies tonight, code deals a Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.

Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks, unless it was role-blocked (R9; set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; a Katana attack counts for its holder, a Kitsune's release for the Kitsune; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).

For each stopped visit, code says it is reflected: resolve it as an Attack of the same level on its attacker (an Astral Visit, never reflected again: a mirror on the attacker just stops it), against their Defense, protection, traps and charms as usual. If it kills, kill with exactly the stopped attack's cause, by the Mirror Maker, katana false (a reflected Katana attack reads as a Katana death); a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Mirror Maker. - Oathsworn: an Oathsworn who spent its token (and wasn't role-blocked) marks its target: use the swear op, which spends the token; it is a visit to the target only, and nothing else happens that night (nobody is told). On the next Night, if the Oathsworn is dead when the Night begins, code says so in tonight's notes: call record_visits first, then the fulfil_oath op ({op:'fulfil_oath', by: <the dead Oathsworn>}): code lists the Divine Attacks, cause 'a blood oath', on the marked player and on every other player who visited them tonight (Astral Visits, not visits; Astral visitors aren't hit). reasoning:
With 8 alive, I'm trying to figure out who's evil - Erin and the Yakuza pair are already accounted for, so I'm turning my attention to Frank's role and whether he fits as part of the remaining threat.

Carol and Frank both claim the same Ivan+Mallory kill, which is suspicious - if Carol is Yakuza she could be faking that claim, and her visiting me N1 raises questions about whether she's Fabricator framing me rather than genuinely innocent. I'm also tracing the Katana's path through Grace to Ivan and wondering if Frank is secretly her teammate given his connection through Ivan's will.

The two quiet nights without a Katana swing bother me - either the wielder is being cautious to avoid detection, or they tried attacking someone protected like me under Alice's trap.

Given the pattern of passive behavior, I'm leaning toward a Vulture or similar quiet neutral rather than Yakuza being the blocker, since those factions tend not to attack every night. Looking at Niaj's repeated watches on Judy with nobody visiting, Dave's tracking results that mostly confirm public information, and Mallory's Saint claim tied to Carol's N4 visit, I'm trying to figure out who's lying versus who's genuinely town based on how their claims corroborate each other.

I need to think through the stall mechanic carefully — tracking which nights and days had confirmed deaths to see how much pressure there really is to hang someone today versus waiting. The real question is whether to hang Olivia: her Cursed claim creates risk either way, since hanging her kills a random Good if she's genuinely Cursed-but-Village, while sparing her risks losing track of information if she's actually a threat.

Looking back at Olivia's Day 2 claim, the oddity of her reported Tracker result (a seemingly random, unverifiable visit) actually reads as more believable for a genuine Roleplayer than a clean, convenient role claim would — though her Cursed claim surfacing only once nominated is still suspicious timing. I'm now cross-checking Dave's tracking claims across nights, noting how his reports often came right after other players' own claims were already public, which makes his information less independently verifiable.

Turning to Carol and Frank, I'm weighing whether Carol could be Yakuza instead of the Enforcer she might claim — her N1 visit to me lines up suspiciously with Grace's attack and could point to a Pharmacist block or Fabricator framing rather than a straightforward kill.

Frank's claim of being Enforcer "since N2" can't be verified, and if he's actually Yakuza, copying Carol's claim after being pressured into an unclaimed corner makes sense. Ivan's will naming Frank as a watch target also looks like it could be a fake Lookout write-up by a Yakuza Ivan trying to muddy the waters.

Comparing the two scenarios: it's a big coincidence if Carol lied and happened to pick exactly Frank's real pair, whereas it's natural if Frank lied by simply copying Carol's earlier claim about Mallory. That makes Frank the more likely liar, pointing to him being Yakuza or neutral, which in turn supports Carol being genuine and the Yakuza core likely including Grace, Ivan, and Frank.

The quiet nights afterward support this — if all three Yakuza are now dead, there's no Katana left to kill, which fits the silence on N3 and N4. If a living Yakuza remained, they'd likely have struck during those nights. That points to the remaining threat being a passive neutral like the Vulture or Arsonist rather than an active killer, since a Werewolf or Serial Killer would probably have acted by now too. I'm leaning toward Arsonist's dousing ability or the Vulture's visiting mechanic as the explanation for the lack of deaths.

I'm weighing suspects for who that Neutral role could be. Olivia's Roleplayer claim is hard to disprove, and Mallory's Saint claim is similarly untestable while also conveniently shielding against hanging, which would make great Vulture cover. Dave's Tracker claims (visits to Judy, Niaj, Mallory, Carol) are unverified by anyone's watch results, so he could plausibly be an Arsonist dousing targets under cover of tracking.

Mallory pushing for hangs today fits either an eager townsperson or a Vulture wanting more bodies to hit that win threshold, so that alone doesn't clear her. Olivia's claimed result matching Carol's real N3 visit is a suspicious coincidence worth flagging if she's faking Roleplayer results.

Checking Olivia's N1 claim against my own actions — I visited nobody, so "Heidi visited Dave" is false, meaning Olivia isn't a genuine tracker reporting real info. That makes me lean toward hanging Dave or Olivia, and since Carol posted her real visit to Mallory before Dave's turn in the order, Dave's claim about tracking Carol to Mallory could theoretically be copied rather than genuine.

Looking further, Dave's claims always come after the relevant info is already public and never risk contradiction — every single result he's given has been "safe," which is a telltale sign of fabrication rather than genuine tracking.

I'll skip posting an N4 audit since there were no votes for D4. My read is Frank is likely Yakuza #3 given the copied pair argument, meaning quiet nights suggest no Yakuza left and the real blocker is a passive Neutral like a Vulture or Arsonist. I want to ask Judy for her N4 result to confirm.

I'm weighing a hang between Olivia and Dave. Mallory's Saint claim is good Vulture cover but can't be hanged, so I'll wait on Judy's result first. There's risk either way: if Olivia's Cursed claim is true she's Village and hanging her costs us two Good players, but if she's lying she could be the Neutral. Dave hanging also risks losing a real tracker. I lean toward suspecting Olivia more since her early Roleplayer self-claim on Day 2, made before any pressure, is unusual for a genuine Village role but would make convenient cover for a Neutral dousing their visits.

Actually a key test: Roleplayer action doesn't register as a visit, so if someone catches Olivia visiting tonight, that proves she's not really a Roleplayer. No one's tracked her yet, so that's a strong move for tonight even if it stalls the clock — and we have Day 6 as backup anyway. I'm considering having Judy track Olivia and Niaj watch Dave simultaneously, then hang with better info on D6; a death overnight would reset the stall clock regardless. Still, the Village lacks a decisive read today, so hanging now might be worth it just to avoid losing a day while we're at eight alive, weighing that against the Vulture's power-up threshold.

Thinking through costs: hanging Olivia if she's truly Cursed and Good means losing two Village-aligned people, dropping us to six with a Neutral still active — a bad outcome. Hanging Dave if he's a real Tracker only costs one Good player, which is the safer bet, and his Day 2 claim still bugs me as suspicious, so I'm leaning toward pushing for Dave while checking with Judy first.

I'm considering that Dave could actually be a Neutral — maybe an Arsonist disguising dousing as "tracking," or even a Vulture given his visit patterns, both of which fit his behavior. I'll keep my message around 120 words to stay within budget, hold off nominating until Judy weighs in, and update my notes accordingly.

My N1 Tracker result clashed with Niaj's Lookout list, but then my N3 result matched Carol's claim, and from then on I couldn't tell whether I was a Roleplayer or a real Tracker with a lying Lookout. The rule says a result "never contradicts a role or alignment that was publicly and truly announced". It isn't clear whether any of my results counted as true announcements here. Since roles are never revealed on death, I think the answer is no, but that could be stated outright. 2) Mirror Maker: the rule says reflected kills are announced with the original cause. That's clear, but it's easy to forget that this makes a dead attacker look like a Katana victim. "If you are dead when the next Night begins (you died that night or during the following Day)" means a mark placed on Night N goes off on Night N+1 if I die on Night N itself, for example to an Enforcer reacting to my Katana attack. I read the role as "mark only before you expect to be hanged" and didn't mark on N2. An Enforcer then killed me that night, so the oath was wasted. A one-line example in the role text would help, such as "mark N2, die N2 → triggers N3". It was also unclear how the mark (a visit) and my Katana attack (another visit) would look to a Tracker or Lookout: as two separate targets, or would the Tracker list both? R6 covers several actions on one target, but not one player visiting two different targets.
output.missing_information: At night I had no easy way to check which claimed roles could punish a Katana attack (Enforcer, Trapper, Mirror Maker) against who was likely to visit me. A reminder in the night prompt, like "a Carol-type Enforcer can hit attackers", is player strategy rather than interface. But a short checklist of my own risk factors, like "you will make an Attack tonight, which roles react to attackers", would have helped. After I died I couldn't see anything, which is expected.
output.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. Everything in the revealed log matched the rules. Mirror reflections were announced under their original causes (Katana, Bounty Hunter). That gave the town a near-certain read on Yakuza on Day 2, which seems a very strong swing from one token. It's within the rules, though.

Keep it, and maybe add a column marking which claims another player's result has independently confirmed. 5) Show the stall-rule countdown (nights or days left before everyone loses) in the ledger, since players spent turns working it out by hand.

3. Consider showing the Ballot Stuffer, or any vote-only role, some hint of its strategic value. Roles that act only during trials are wasted if the player dies on Night 1, which happened here.
4. On hand-picked setups, a one-line public hint such as "protective roles exist" would make Night 1 kill choices less of a coin flip.

answers.confusing_rules: Oathsworn timing took me a while to work out. "If you are dead when the next Night begins (you died that night or during the following Day)" means a mark placed on Night N goes off on Night N+1 if I die on Night N itself, for example to an Enforcer reacting to my Katana attack. I read the role as "mark only before you expect to be hanged" and didn't mark on N2. An Enforcer then killed me that night, so the oath was wasted. A one-line example in the role text would help, such as "mark N2, die N2 → triggers N3". It was also unclear how the mark (a visit) and my Katana attack (another visit) would look to a Tracker or Lookout: as two separate targets, or would the Tracker list both? R6 covers several actions on one target, but not one player visiting two different targets.

But a short checklist of my own risk factors, like "you will make an Attack tonight, which roles react to attackers", would have helped. After I died I couldn't see anything, which is expected.

Things I checked after the reveal: the trial totals were consistent with the traits (D3: 7 Guilty / 2 Innocent = Frank and Heidi Merciful, Dave Zealot. D5: 7 / 1 = Heidi Merciful, Dave's Zealot vote counted Guilty in his own trial). Bob's mirror on me N2 stopping 0 attacks while Dave doused me is correct, since a douse isn't an attack. Olivia's Roleplayer result "Carol visited Olivia" on N3 happened to be true by chance, which made her claim look odd but follows R24.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add a stall-clock line to the public ledger: "a death is needed by Night X or everyone loses". 2) Add a per-trial vote sheet to the ledger: each player's stated vote next to the announced totals, plus publicly claimed vote-changing traits. 3) Give a short public reminder of which Neutral headings are possible in hand-picked setups, or at least say "a passive Neutral may be keeping the game alive". 4) Keep the claims summary in the ledger, which was very useful.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Roleplayer: the role can only be worked out by cross-checking other players' claims. My N1 Tracker result clashed with Niaj's Lookout list, but then my N3 result matched Carol's claim, and from then on I couldn't tell whether I was a Roleplayer or a real Tracker with a lying Lookout. The rule says a result "never contradicts a role or alignment that was publicly and truly announced". It isn't clear whether any of my results counted as true announcements here. Since roles are never revealed on death, I think the answer is no, but that could be stated outright. 2) Mirror Maker: the rule says reflected kills are announced with the original cause. That's clear, but it's easy to forget that this makes a dead attacker look like a Katana victim. A short example in the rules would help. 3) Stall rule (R14): "three previous Nights and three previous Days" made it hard to count the deadline precisely. We worked out "need a death by N6", but a worked example would help.
answers.missing_information: The ledger lists claims, but not stated votes next to the announced totals. I had to do that reconciliation myself in my notepad: who said Yes/Guilty, and whose traits (Merciful, Zealot) change the count. A per-trial table showing "claimed votes vs total" would make vote analysis much easier. I also had no record of who was doused or targeted where, beyond my own results.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. I checked the final totals against the revealed traits. Frank's trial was 7G/2I, with Heidi and Frank both Merciful. Dave's trial was 7G/1I, with Heidi Merciful and Dave's own Zealot vote counting Guilty. Both are consistent. My Roleplayer results were plausibly random: N3 matched by chance and N4 didn't. Carol's N3 Strong double on Dave correctly gave "no attack", because Dave was dousing and a douse isn't an attack.
answers.suggestions: Add a vote-reconciliation view to the public ledger: each trial's total next to the vote each player stated. Add a short glossary of common deductions, such as "a mirror makes the attacker die of their own cause" and "an Enforcer kill means the target attacked that night". Show the stall-rule deadline explicitly each morning ("a death is needed by Night X"). For Roleplayers, consider a note in the rules that a self-claimed Roleplayer can't be distinguished from a real investigator except by cross-checks, so players treat the claim with suitable caution.

answers.confusing_rules:
1) Who makes a reflected attack (Mirror Maker). N1, Bob's mirror on Heidi reflected Grace's Katana attack and Erin's Bounty Hunter attack back at them. The rules don't say who counts as the source of a reflection: the original attacker, the mirrored player (Heidi) or the Mirror Maker. That matters for:
- Bloodhound counts ("Attacks made")
- an Enforcer visiting the mirrored player (Carol visited Heidi that night; I ruled Heidi made no attack)
- Avenger and Decoy naming
- Bounty Hunter claims
I ruled that a reflection counts as an attack by nobody's choice and isn't credited to Heidi. Erin's bounty on Grace was lost because Grace died of her own reflected Katana, not of Erin's attack.

2) Two Enforcers hitting the same player. N2, Carol and Frank both picked Ivan + Mallory and both landed a Basic on Ivan. R12 suggests every fatal cause counts, so I told both "your attack killed". The Enforcer text doesn't say this directly. The Hitman text does say "counts even if another fatal Attack hit them too". The same rule should be stated generally.

3) Token wording. The Mirror Maker's "spend a token" is listed in the action log as an optional choice ("chose to spend 1 token(s)"). In fact a mirror always costs a token. The same applies to the Bounty Hunter's single attack. The log makes a cost look like a choice.

4) Bounty Hunter losing while dead. After N1 Erin was dead with 0 tokens, so she could never claim 2 bounties. The rules only describe the reveal-and-leave for a living Bounty Hunter. Whether a dead Bounty Hunter gets a private "you lost" message isn't specified. I sent nothing.
answers.missing_information:

- There was no running state view for: Dave's douse set (Judy, Niaj, Mallory, Carol), Alice's trap location and armed status, token counts per player (Carol's went 3→2→0, Bob's 2→1→0), and Ivan's unused oath token.

answers.wanted_but_couldnt:

answers.bugs_or_oddities:

R3 says a target hit by several attacks learns the role behind each. The message merged them into one. Compare Heidi on N1, who correctly got both Katana and Bounty Hunter listed.

answers.suggestions:
- Add a moderator state panel: Katana holder, tokens per player, traps (placed/armed), douse lists, bounty and Executioner targets, oath marks, trait triggers pending.
- Write one notification line per attack when a player is hit by several attacks, including duplicates of the same role ("attacked by an Enforcer, an Enforcer").
- Add a rule clause saying who a reflected or stopped attack is credited to (for Enforcer, Bloodhound, Avenger, Decoy, Bounty Hunter and Hitman). Also make "each fatal attack counts as a kill" a general rule instead of putting it only in the Hitman's text.
- Log mandatory token costs as costs, not as "chose to spend".

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Ignite the first night you have 2-3 living players doused, especially if they include confirmed investigators. Each extra night of dousing is one more Day you can be hanged, and every douse is lost if you die. Four nights of dousing and no ignite meant I died with four players doused.

lessons.applies_to: Neutral or Yakuza faking an investigator
lessons.tip: A fake Tracker or Lookout whose results only repeat facts that are already public gets read as 'never risked anything' and becomes the stall-clock rope. Post at least one result before the fact it confirms becomes public. You can also pick a cover whose results nobody can check but that still gives new information.

When nobody has died for two nights, the stall rule pushes the town to hang the least-tested active claim even with no break. If you are a hidden killer, act (kill or ignite) before that pressure builds, so the town has fresh leads to chase.

A Roleplayer's random result can come out true by chance. Olivia's random 'Dave visited Niaj' was actually where I went. If a self-declared Roleplayer names your real visit, don't call it noise too loudly. Make sure your own claimed target can't be contradicted by a real watcher.

Zealot makes your own trial vote count Guilty against you. On your own trial you need one more Innocent from other players. Lobby early and in public, before the nomination, rather than through last-minute PMs that look like pressure.

tips_feedback.tip: Arsonist: ignite once three players are doused, or sooner if questioned.
tips_feedback.why: It was correct and I didn't follow it. After N3 I had Judy, Niaj and Mallory doused. Igniting on N4 would have left about 5 players with me in a strong spot. I doused again instead and was hanged D5.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Mayor, Vulture and Hitman are Unique, so both claimants of any other role can be real. Test both claimants rather than hanging one on the clash.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Frank were both real Enforcers. The town hanged Frank on the duplicate anyway and lost a Village power role, which shows the tip is right.

tips_feedback.tip: Pick one consistent tokenless cover early. If you survive an attack, don't admit it under a claim with no Defense of its own.
tips_feedback.why: My Tracker cover stayed consistent, but because every result confirmed public facts, it became the case against me. Being consistent wasn't enough. The cover also needed results that took some risk.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: my main mistake was waiting too long to ignite.

reasoning:
Looking back as Arsonist, I doused four players over four nights without ever igniting, and got hanged on day five for it. The lesson is clear: I should have ignited once three were doused by night three, which would've killed Judy and Niaj instead of letting myself get caught.

My Tracker cover also failed because it only confirmed public info, which gave town the ammo to hang me — a lesson that fake investigator claims need either a pre-committed prediction or an unfalsifiable role to avoid suspicion. I also noticed Olivia's "random" tracker result actually matched true events by coincidence, and that town hanged Frank despite both Enforcer claims potentially being real, showing town sometimes ignores good mechanical reasoning under pressure to convict.

lessons.tip: On Night 1, don't send the Katana at the loudest Day 1 organizer. Town protectors expect that and stack on them: here a Mirror, a Trapper, an Enforcer and three investigators all visited the same player. A mirror reflects the attack and kills your holder. Hit a quiet player instead.

The Katana holder's cover has to explain a visit to the attack target. A no-visit cover like Fortune Teller gets disproven as soon as a Lookout lists you as a visitor. Use a visiting role (Tracker, Lookout, Medic) and write a will that names the target as your visit.

If you hold the Katana on a night when an Enforcer, Veteran or reflector could be active, spend the oath that same night. It only fires if you die, so it costs nothing if you survive, and it lapses if you die without having marked anyone. Saving it 'for later' wasted it.

A death whose cause matches an attack the same night's survivor also suffered (Katana victim, Katana death) usually means a reflection. Ask for Lookout lists on the survivor. The dead attacker's will is the lie to check.

With only 2 Yakuza, losing the holder on N1 leaves one player alone against a town full of active roles. Weigh survival over the first kill: a turn with no attack, or a low-risk target, is often better than a kill attempt on the most-protected player.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't hint at a power role, and don't be the loudest organizer. That voice is usually the Night 1 Katana target.
tips_feedback.why: It helped the town. The town treated Heidi as the obvious N1 target and piled protection on her, and my Katana attack on her was mirrored back and killed me. For Yakuza, going after the organizer was predictable.

tips_feedback.tip: On Night 1, agree a Village cover for each member that fits their tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: I broke the 'fits real visits' part myself. As holder I claimed a no-visit Fortune Teller, and Niaj's Lookout list showed me visiting Heidi, which disproved my will at once. Ivan's Lookout will was also exposed by Judy's track and Niaj's watch.

tips_feedback.tip: Treat a lone visitor to a Katana victim as near-proof only when a second source corroborates it.
tips_feedback.why: Judy's track and Niaj's watch independently placed Ivan at Bob, and the Enforcer kill backed them up. That locked in Ivan as the holder with no doubt left.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens at the first night or Day they can change a vote, because they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan held his once-only oath token for later and died on N2 without using it. Both of my ballot tokens also died unused. Following the tip would have mattered.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: the N1 attack on the obvious target was mirrored, the cover didn't fit my visits, and the oath was never used.

reasoning:
I should draw lessons from the Katana attack on Day 1's loudest organizer getting mirrored back—better to target someone less obvious or use a holder whose loss matters less. Also my FT will got disproven instantly by the Lookout list, so I'm noting that a cover story with no visits is risky for a Katana holder, since a Lookout watching the target would catch the visit.

Another missed opportunity: Ivan never used his oath mark before dying—Oathsworn holding the Katana should mark someone on the night they attack, since that's the risky window and the mark lapses if they stay alive. On the tips side, the advice to avoid being the loudest organizer helped protect town but made the predictable target for protectors to stack on; meanwhile treating a lone visitor claim as near-proof worked well once corroborated by two other players.

lessons.tip: A claimed investigator whose every result only confirms facts that were already public, and never names anything new, is a strong fake-claim sign. Neutrals such as an Arsonist do this because they really visit someone each night and need a cover. Put pressure on them before the stall clock does.

Don't watch the same 'safe' target night after night. Watch the target a suspect claims to be tracking, or a player nobody claims to visit. An Arsonist's douse is a visit and only shows up if you watch the player being doused. Watching the same quiet player twice told me nothing.

Quiet nights with no deaths, while the game still hasn't ended, point to a passive blocking Neutral, usually an Arsonist dousing. Good players are never told they were doused. List every claimed visitor whose visits nobody else has confirmed, and hang the most suspect one before the Arsonist ignites.

When two players claim the same non-unique role, test them before hanging. Two Enforcers who both name the same unclaimed pair is quite likely, because there are few unclaimed players to choose from. A matching result is not proof that one of them copied the other.

If a Lookout's visitor list leaves out a player who claims to have visited, that player is probably a Roleplayer, and their results are noise. Don't let an untestable claim that a player volunteered, like Roleplayer or Cursed, push the vote onto them on its own. Weigh what the claim cost them to make.

If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

lessons.tip: A second claimant of a non-unique role who posts the same targets as the first is not proof of a copy. Two real players with the same role tend to pick the same targets when only a few players are unclaimed. If the stall clock allows, test the duplicate overnight with a track or watch before you hang them.

Look for an investigator whose every result was already public before they posted it (tracking a player who has already posted their target, or confirming a list that was already posted). That pattern fits a Neutral or Yakuza faking results. Hang that claim over an untestable but harmless one such as a Roleplayer, especially when the untestable claimant also says Cursed.

Quiet nights with nobody attacked and no traps going off point to an Arsonist who is still dousing. Good players are never told they were doused, so a quiet passive Neutral is easy to miss. Hang a suspect soon, before it ignites.

When the Mirror Maker reflects attacks, each attacker dies with the cause of their own attack. So a Katana death on the attacker's side shows the Katana holder, and a Bounty Hunter death shows the Bounty Hunter. Match causes of death to visitor lists to identify the attackers for certain.

If you hold a trait that changes how your vote counts, announce it and do the vote math out loud ('5 of the other 7 must vote Guilty'). Also keep in mind that another player can really hold the same trait. Frank's Merciful claim was true, and I wrongly treated it as convenient.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Mayor, Vulture and Hitman are Unique, so both claimants of any other role can be real. Test both claimants rather than hanging one on the clash.

lessons.tip: Don't leave a trap sitting on the Day 1 organizer for the rest of the game. You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.applies_to: everyone with a result that explains a death (Enforcer, Vigilante, Tracker, etc.)
lessons.tip: If your night result explains a public death, post your full claim (role, target(s), exact result, tokens left) on your first turn the next Day. If a second claimant posts the same result first, yours looks copied, and 'I claimed last' becomes the whole case for hanging you.

Don't say 'my result is in my will' while staying unclaimed. It shows you have an active role without giving the town anything it can verify. Other players plan around you, and later it is used as proof that you were hiding. Either claim in full or say nothing.

lessons.applies_to: Enforcer (and any role with a duplicate copy in play)
lessons.tip: Avoid the obvious target set, such as 'the unclaimed players'. Another copy of your role will probably pick the same pair, and the identical result then reads as a copied claim. A slightly off-pattern second target gives you a result that is uniquely yours and can be checked.

lessons.applies_to: Village players about to be hanged
lessons.tip: In your final words and will, don't point at a claimant whose results have outside support, like Carol's Lookout-confirmed visit and audit. That only misleads the town after you die. Point to the claims nobody has tested, such as trackers whose results only repeat what is already public. That heuristic caught the Arsonist here.

An investigator whose every result only confirms facts that were already public, and never risks anything new, is a strong Neutral or Yakuza lead. It is worth a hang under stall pressure when nothing else breaks.

tips_feedback.tip: Only Mayor, Vulture and Hitman are Unique, so both claimants of any other role can be real. Test both claimants rather than hanging one on the clash.
tips_feedback.why: The tip was correct. Both Enforcer claims were real, but the town ignored the tip and hanged me, a Village Enforcer, on the duplicate alone. That cost the Village a player.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked.
tips_feedback.why: I stayed unclaimed through Day 2 and was the last to claim on Day 3. The delay became the main case against me, which confirms the tip.

tips_feedback.tip: On Day 1 and Day 2, don't hint at a power role.
tips_feedback.why: My Day 2 line 'my result so far is in my will' was a hint. Carol used it to choose her targets, which produced the duplicate pair, and Heidi cited it against me.

tips_feedback.tip: Treat a lone visitor to a Katana victim as near-proof only when a second source corroborates it.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan as the Katana holder was backed by Judy's track, Niaj's watch and the Enforcer death. The town read it correctly.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately... keep a written list of suspects.
tips_feedback.why: The town picked out Dave (the Arsonist, posing as a Tracker whose results only repeated public facts) as the least-tested claim and hanged him before he could ignite.

output.reason: These are reflections on the game: my late claim and duplicate Enforcer result got me hanged, and the town still found the Arsonist.

reasoning:

The lesson is clear: when a result bears directly on a death, claim it at the very first opportunity rather than holding it in reserve.

I should've avoided accusing Carol, a corroborated claimant, and instead pointed suspicion toward less-checked, unclaimed players. And for duplicate Enforcer claims, picking a less obvious target pair would've helped avoid looking like a copy. The tip about testing both claimants was correct but town didn't follow it, which cost them a real Enforcer even though they still won.

My delayed claim across two days became part of the suspicion against me, so answering directly the first time I was asked would've helped. Dropping a hint about having a "result in my will" was a mistake — Carol used it to pick targets and Heidi used it against me, which clearly hurt my case. On the positive side, treating Ivan as a lone visitor turned out fine since his claim got corroborated by multiple deaths, and the advice to actively hunt neutral killers paid off when Dave the Arsonist was hanged.

lessons.applies_to: Roleplayer / anyone told they hold an Investigative role
lessons.tip: Check your own visits against a trusted Lookout or Tracker result on the same target. If a well-corroborated visitor list leaves you out, you are almost certainly a Roleplayer. lessons.applies_to: Players with a costly-to-hang trait (Cursed, Saint-like effects)
lessons.tip: Once your trait is in your will, reveal it publicly the moment you are named as a rope target. A real cost to the Village, like Cursed taking two Good players, can turn a nomination that is about to happen onto a better suspect.

When two players claim the same non-unique role with matching results, check whether both had the same small pool of targets, such as the only unclaimed players. If they did, matching picks are likely, and a duplicate means very little. Here a real Village Enforcer was hanged on 'he copied her', when testing him for one night would have been cheap.

If your results may be random, post them before the person they concern speaks. That makes them a clean test. A match never proves the claim, but a mismatch keeps pressure on a claimant nobody has tested.

lessons.tip: Arsonist douses aren't attacks, so an Enforcer can't catch an Arsonist on dousing nights, and an empty Katana night gives you nothing to catch either. Don't burn Strong or double tokens on quiet nights. Save them for nights when someone is likely to swing, such as right after a failed attack or a reflected kill.

In hand-picked setups, duplicate Village power roles are common. Two Enforcers can pick the same pair because the pool of unclaimed players is small. Before calling the second claimant a copier, ask what they could not have copied: an earlier target, a private detail, or a target written in their will before the night. A late claim alone shouldn't decide the hang.

A claimed investigator whose every result only confirms something already public (tracking players right after they announce their target, or getting 'visited nobody' on actionless claims) is a strong sign of a fake claim. In this game that was the Arsonist. Ask investigators to write their target in their will before the night, so later results can be checked against a commitment.

Several quiet nights while the game keeps going, including a full moon, point to an Arsonist dousing. Good players are never told they were doused. Hang the most suspicious fake-confirming claim before the ignite rather than waiting out the stall clock.

When you post a full result (pair, result wording, token count) before an unclaimed player with the same role speaks, the second claimant can no longer be tested against it. If duplicates are possible, post your target first and ask the other player for their pair and wording before you give yours.

reasoning:
We won the game, so now I'm pulling out the key lessons: claiming Saint early protected against rope votes, especially combined with track evidence showing no visits, and a tracker whose reports only confirm already-known facts turned out to be a tell that Dave was the fake Arsonist. I'm also noting that Frank's duplicate claim, copying details after someone else posted, raised suspicion of lying.

Actually Frank turned out to be a genuine Village Enforcer, and his claim was true even though it matched Carol's — so duplicate claims with the same pairing aren't automatically fake. We violated the "test both claimants before hanging one" rule, hanging a Village Enforcer unnecessarily, though it didn't cost us the game; Frank's N1 visit detail on Ivan was something Carol couldn't have fabricated. I'm also working through the trial vote totals, since Dave was secretly a Zealot whose vote counted as Guilty despite claiming otherwise, which shifted the 7-1 tally in a way that should have been a clue.

Olivia's Roleplayer claim turned out honest specifically because her result contradicted the Lookout's list and she still admitted to being a Roleplayer — a useful tell for genuine claims. I'm also noting that Dave, an Arsonist, doused several players without igniting and cleverly faked being a Tracker by visiting the exact same targets he claimed to be tracking, which let him slip past Lookout verification entirely — a trick worth remembering for future games.

On the tips review, the "test unique roles" advice was actually correct but ignored, costing Frank's life as the real Enforcer, so I'm marking that one ambiguous between hurt/helped since following it would have saved him. The "stall near the lock" and "post full results" tips both get marked as helped, since they led to successful hangs and clearer identification of suspects like Grace and Erin.

I'm also noting the Katana victim corroboration tip helped confirm Ivan, and the N1 loudest-organizer prediction accurately flagged Heidi as a target, so that counts as helped too. For the notepad, I'll leave it empty for now and keep the other fields blank.

lessons.tip: Don't leave a trap sitting on the Day 1 organizer for the rest of the game. After the Day 2 claims, move it to the most valuable player who just outed themselves (a Mirror Maker or confirmed investigator who is now the obvious Katana target). A trap that would have stopped the N2 Katana attack on Bob would also have hit the holder back with a Strong Attack.

When two players claim the same non-unique role with matching results, check whether the second claim adds something only a real holder could know (a different N1 target, a different order of targets in a pair). Frank named a separate N1 target and was a real Enforcer, and hanging him on a 'copy' story wasted a rope.

A claimed Tracker or Lookout whose results only ever confirm facts that were already public, and never come out first, is a strong fake-investigator sign. It fits a Neutral killer (an Arsonist dousing) inventing safe results. Ask them to post their result before the player they tracked posts theirs.

Quiet nights while the game goes on, after the likely Yakuza count is used up, point to a passive Neutral (an Arsonist dousing, or a Vulture). Good players are never told they were doused, so list every claimant whose visits are uncorroborated and hang among them before the stall clock runs out.

Track the stall clock out loud (no death in 3 Nights and 3 Days means everyone loses). It justifies hanging the least-tested active claim when no break exists, and it beats waiting for a perfect break.

lessons.applies_to: Mirror Maker, Medic and other protectors
lessons.tip: If someone else has already put forward the protection explanation for a survival (here a Yakuza did, to draw out the protector), don't confirm it publicly in your own name. On Night 1, protect the loudest Day 1 organizer. On Night 2, after a public reveal, the Yakuza will go after the revealed protector or investigators, not the player you guarded before. Pick your ward on the assumption that you are now the bait.

An investigator whose results only ever confirm facts that were already public (tracking a claimed visitor, or someone who has already posted their target) has risked nothing. Treat them as a likely fake cover for a Neutral, such as an Arsonist dousing quietly. Ask for targets to be committed in the will before the night.

When two players claim the same non-unique killing role with the same result, check whether the role's result wording allows both to be true. Two Enforcers who both visited the same pair get identical results. Test them with a track or audit instead of hanging the one who claimed later.

No deaths on several nights while the game goes on means a non-killing blocker is still alive (an Arsonist dousing, a Vulture, a passive Yakuza). Keep the stall count public and give the rope to the least-verified active claim before the deadline.

lessons.tip: Arsonist douses aren't attacks, so an Enforcer can't catch an Arsonist on dousing nights, and an empty Katana night gives you nothing to catch either. In hand-picked setups, duplicate Village power roles are common. Two Enforcers can pick the same pair because the pool of unclaimed players is small. Before calling the second claimant a copier, ask what they could not have copied: an earlier target, a private detail, or a target written in their will before the night. A late claim alone shouldn't decide the hang.

A claimed investigator whose every result only confirms something already public (tracking players right after they announce their target, or getting 'visited nobody' on actionless claims) is a strong sign of a fake claim. Several quiet nights while the game keeps going, including a full moon, point to an Arsonist dousing. Good players are never told they were doused. Hang the most suspicious fake-confirming claim before the ignite rather than waiting out the stall clock.

When you post a full result (pair, result wording, token count) before an unclaimed player with the same role speaks, the second claimant can no longer be tested against it. If duplicates are possible, post your target first and ask the other player for their pair and wording before you give yours.

Zealot makes your own trial vote count Guilty against you. On your own trial you need one more Innocent from other players. Lobby early and in public, before the nomination, rather than through last-minute PMs that look like pressure.

lessons.tip: A 'Tracker' whose every result only confirms facts already public (a Lookout's list, a target someone else already posted) is the top suspect for a Neutral killer using a fake claim. An Arsonist can visit (douse) the same player it claims to track, so a Lookout watching that player sees nothing odd. Ask that claimant to post tonight's target before the Day's other results come out, or watch its claimed target with a second Tracker.

Two players claiming the same non-unique role with the same night pair can both be real, because unclaimed players are an obvious shared target list. Before hanging the later claimant, check whether they gave a detail the first claimant never posted (e.g. a different N1 target). If they did, test them at night instead of hanging them.

Quiet nights with no deaths and nobody saying they survived an attack point to a passive blocker: an Arsonist dousing, a Vulture, or a team that has run out of Yakuza. Once the visit-based results agree, hunt the claim whose visits nobody has checked independently. Don't assume a Yakuza is hiding.

Claim Saint plainly as soon as you're asked for a claim, and invite tracks on yourself. Two 'visited nobody' tracks backed the claim, and after that nobody seriously pushed a rope on me. Then spend your voice pushing the hang onto the real suspect, so the Day doesn't drift toward the one claim nobody can check.

Before a trial, work out the expected totals from the claimed vote-modifying traits (Merciful, Zealot). If the result is one Guilty more than expected, a hidden Zealot is the likeliest cause, and it is often the nominee themself.

lessons.tip: A claimed investigator whose every result only confirms facts that were already public, and never names anything new, is a strong fake-claim sign. Neutrals such as an Arsonist do this because they really visit someone each night and need a cover. Put pressure on them before the stall clock does.

Don't watch the same 'safe' target night after night. Watch the target a suspect claims to be tracking, or a player nobody claims to visit. An Arsonist's douse is a visit and only shows up if you watch the player being doused. Watching the same quiet player twice told me nothing.

Quiet nights with no deaths, while the game still hasn't ended, point to a passive blocking Neutral, usually an Arsonist dousing. Good players are never told they were doused. List every claimed visitor whose visits nobody else has confirmed, and hang the most suspect one before the Arsonist ignites.

When two players claim the same non-unique role, test them before hanging. Two Enforcers who both name the same unclaimed pair is quite likely, because there are few unclaimed players to choose from. A matching result is not proof that one of them copied the other.

If a Lookout's visitor list leaves out a player who claims to have visited, that player is probably a Roleplayer, and their results are noise. Don't let an untestable claim that a player volunteered, like Roleplayer or Cursed, push the vote onto them on its own. Weigh what the claim cost them to make.

lessons.applies_to: Roleplayer / anyone told they hold an Investigative role
lessons.tip: Check your own visits against a trusted Lookout or Tracker result on the same target. If a well-corroborated visitor list leaves you out, you are almost certainly a Roleplayer. Say so early and tell the town to ignore your results. Then you never feed the town noise, and you can't be framed as a liar later.

Look for an investigator whose results only ever confirm facts that were already public: a list someone posted, a claim someone made, or a 'visited nobody' on a no-action claim. That pattern fits a Neutral or Yakuza faking a tracking role, and here it was the Arsonist. Ask them to post results before the claims they would confirm come out, or track them yourself.

lessons.applies_to: Players with a costly-to-hang trait (Cursed, Saint-like effects)
lessons.tip: Once your trait is in your will, reveal it publicly the moment you are named as a rope target. A real cost to the Village, like Cursed taking two Good players, can turn a nomination that is about to happen onto a better suspect.

When two players claim the same non-unique role with matching results, check whether both had the same small pool of targets, such as the only unclaimed players. If they did, matching picks are likely, and a duplicate means very little. Here a real Village Enforcer was hanged on 'he copied her', when testing him for one night would have been cheap.

If your results may be random, post them before the person they concern speaks. That makes them a clean test. A match never proves the claim, but a mismatch keeps pressure on a claimant nobody has tested.

tips_feedback.why: Heidi organized on Day 1 and took the Katana and the Bounty Hunter attack on N1, just as predicted. Protectors who expected this (Bob's mirror) killed both attackers.
