summary: The Village won. The game was mostly decided in the first two nights. On Day 1 Heidi organized loudly, and the Yakuza (Grace and Ivan) picked her as the Night 1 target, as nearly everyone expected. Six players visited her. Bob's mirror on her stopped both Grace's Katana attack and Erin's Strong Bounty Hunter shot and sent each back, so both attackers died. Niaj's visitor list then exposed Grace's fake 'Fortune Teller' will, because a Fortune Teller never visits. On Night 2 Ivan held the Katana and killed Bob. That night both Enforcers, Carol and Frank, spent a token to visit the same two unclaimed players, Ivan and Mallory, and killed Ivan. Ivan still had his Oathsworn token, so the Yakuza were gone after two nights and their last-ditch tool was never used. The Village then made a big mistake. They hanged Frank, a real Enforcer, because he claimed last and his pair, result and token count matched Carol's. That was a duplicate claim of a role that isn't unique, not a mechanical break, and Ivan's fake will had pointed at him. Only one hidden killer was left, the Arsonist Dave, so the mis-hang didn't cost the game. Dave doused Judy, Niaj, Mallory and Carol but never ignited. A Night 4 ignite would have killed three doused Village players, and Judy is Cursed, so her death would have killed one more. Instead he kept a fake Tracker claim whose results only ever repeated facts that were already public. With the stall clock running, Mallory counted it out and Heidi, Mallory and Niaj built a case on his 'risk-free' results. The town hanged him on Day 5, and the Village won.

lessons.applies_to: Village protectors (Mirror Maker, Medic, Trapper, Kitsune)
lessons.tip: On Night 1, protect the loudest Day 1 organizer. Yakuza with no information usually hit that player first. A mirror or charm there can also kill or reveal the attackers. Don't announce it.
lessons.evidence: Grace's night chat picked Heidi because 'she set up the vote-tracking'. Bob's mirror on Heidi stopped both the Katana and the Bounty Hunter shot and sent them back, killing Grace and Erin on Night 1.

lessons.tip: Don't send the Night 1 Katana at the most obvious town leader, because protectors pile onto that player. Pick a quieter player who seems capable. Never write a fake will for a role that doesn't visit when you plan to visit someone that night: a Lookout or Tracker will contradict it.
lessons.evidence: Six players visited Heidi on Night 1. The mirror killed Grace with her own Katana, and Niaj's list showing Grace as a visitor broke her 'Fortune Teller (no visits)' will on Day 2.

lessons.tip: An Enforcer only hits players who attacked that night, so it can't hurt quiet Village roles. Spend a token on a double visit to the unclaimed players most likely to hold the Katana. Post your exact pair and result as soon as it matters, so a second Enforcer's matching claim can be checked against yours.
lessons.evidence: On Night 2 Carol and Frank both visited the unclaimed Ivan and Mallory. Both hit Ivan, the Katana holder who had just killed Bob, and that ended the Yakuza. Mallory, who made no attack, was untouched.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza (Oathsworn, and any Katana holder facing claimed Enforcers)
lessons.tip: Spend a one-shot revenge token like the oath on any night you could plausibly die, especially when you're the last Yakuza holding the Katana, you haven't claimed, and an Enforcer is known. If you're unclaimed while an Enforcer hunts unclaimed players, either claim something or hold the attack that night.
lessons.evidence: Carol publicly claimed Enforcer on Day 2, and Ivan stayed one of three unclaimed players. He attacked Bob anyway, died to two Enforcer visits, and his oath token went unused. A mark on Judy or Niaj could have taken them and their visitors down too.

lessons.tip: Two players claiming the same role that isn't unique, with matching results, is not a break. Check whether the results are mechanically consistent. Two Enforcers both hitting Ivan and both missing Mallory fits two real Enforcers. Test both claimants that night instead of hanging one, and remember that a dead Yakuza's fake will often points at the player they want hanged.
lessons.evidence: On Day 3 the town hanged Frank 7-2 for 'copying' Carol. He was a real Village Enforcer. Ivan's fake will had named Frank. Judy even said 'a duplicate isn't a mechanical break' and then voted Guilty.

lessons.applies_to: Village with a non-unique or easily copied role
lessons.tip: Claim and post your full results early, in public and in your will. A claim that appears only after a matching one is public looks copied, however true it is.
lessons.evidence: Frank delayed on Day 2 ('I'll claim fully on Day 3 if anyone asks'). He then claimed after Carol had posted her pair, result and tokens, and the whole case against him was the timing.

lessons.tip: Ignite once three or more players are doused, and earlier if a fake claim is under pressure. Every extra douse night adds risk and kills nothing. Dousing a Cursed player is extra value, because the curse adds a death when they burn.
lessons.evidence: By the end of Night 3 Dave had doused Judy, Niaj and Mallory. He doused Carol on Night 4 instead of igniting and was hanged on Day 5 with four doused players alive. Igniting on Night 4 would have killed Judy, Niaj and Mallory, and Judy's curse would have killed another Good player.

lessons.applies_to: Evil or Neutral players faking an investigator
lessons.tip: A fake result that only repeats facts already public reads as risk-free and becomes the case against you. Fake checks on targets nobody else is covering, or pick a cover whose results are naturally empty.
lessons.evidence: Every one of Dave's Tracker results (Judy to Heidi, Niaj to Bob, Mallory to nobody, Carol to Mallory) came after the fact it 'confirmed' was public. Mallory and Niaj used exactly that to hang him under the stall clock.

tips_feedback.why: The one Village mis-hang (Frank, Day 3) came from ignoring the break requirement. The Day 5 hang of Dave followed the 'near the lock, hang the best case' clause under the stall rule, and it ended the game.

issues.description: All 13 players were given tips/tips.md even though the harness flagged it (ERROR tips_stale) as last checked against an older version of the rules, so some tips may be wrong. I saw no tip that misled anyone in this game, but the file should be revised before more games use it.

Night 1 has two [Moderator summary] entries with the same content in slightly different wording (the second ends 'Code passes the Katana to Ivan'). It looks like the summary step ran twice or the output was logged twice. It doesn't affect the game, but it could confuse whatever reads the log later.
